chapter: The circus dream and choosing the clarinet
title: The steam calliope on the circus parade wagon
summary: His uncle warns him off violin and piano; Joe explains how the steam calliope worked and why its players often went deaf.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did your father and your uncle kind of... Did your respond to you wanting to go with the circus? Did they argue and say, 'The boy should stay here and do this'...?

That's what my uncle used to tell me. 'You stay here and do like your father says. You learn to fix shoes. And when you get old enough, I'll take you on a circus with me. But look, you forget about that violin and piano.' Because they didn't have any piano on a circus, and certainly didn't have violin. The only thing close to a piano is that steam calliope; that's what they called it in those days. They called them calliopes now.
Up North they call them calliopes, and down South most of them use...
A few of the boats still have them.
Darensbourg - 10
There's one out on the Mississippi now around the bend where the Jackspur(?) used to be?
What is the boat that docked there near St. Louis?
The President?
Yes. They have one on that.
That one plays in New Orleans every Sunday morning now. Nice. Great sound.

I remember when we played a concert on that boat in St. Louis, and I seen that calliope, and I went up on deck and talked to the guy. But they used to run them on steam in those days. Incidentally, that's why that was the last wagon in a circus parade. Horses pulled those wagons in those days. And that was literally a steam boiler, because it took steam to run those pitch pipes that made your sound.
You mean the calliope was on the same wagon that the pipes...
That's right. It was a big, big, big steam tank.
Well, where did the man sit and play it?
The guys used to sit right up in front of it on this wagon. And there was a guy in the back, and they called them stokers -- used to keep that fire going to keep
Darensbourg - 11
that steam going. And it was a dangerous thing.
This was when the circus would parade through the town that it would be playing.
Right.
But they never used it in the circus band, or did they, in the Big Top...

Not when I was with the circus. In later years, more (?) with the Ringling Brothers Circus. But it was run by electric power, the same as all of them is today. But coming back to that confounded... My uncle said, "Look, Joe, those things is pretty dangerous, and most guys that play those things go deaf."
Is that right?
You could hear those things forever...
Oh, I know, you can hear them. All over New Orleans today you can hear them.
